why: This run launched before e3ad28e, so its credit_balance_at_launch came from the ACCOUNT-ONLY guard, which read /credits and never the key's own remaining allowance. The run was deliberately NOT restarted to pick up the fix.
guard_from_e3ad28e: min(account balance, key limit_remaining), naming the binding limit
was_the_recorded_figure_correct_at_launc: YES. At launch the account held about $800 and the key's $1,000 limit was almost unused, so the account WAS the binding limit and the account-only guard returned the binding figure. The method became unsafe only after the $500 top-up made the key bind: account $1,127.35 against key $826.40.
risk_while_this_run_continues: Exhausting the key returns HTTP 402, which llm_policy raises as CreditsExhausted, halting the run and abandoning the in-flight campaign UNWRITTEN. The failure mode is a clean halt and not contaminated data; the floor check would simply not have warned in advance.
